chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn Mukhtar al-Hamdani, from al-Fath ibn Yazid al-Jurjani, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the least that is required for recognition, so he said: 'The affirmation that there is no god other than Him, and that He has no peer or rival, and that He is Eternal, Established, Existing, not confined, and that there is nothing whatsoever like unto Him.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْء: There is nothing like unto Him

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum level of knowledge required to recognize God's unity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as the foundational threshold of *ma'rifah*, emphasizing that true recognition of God begins with affirming His absolute uniqueness (*tawhid*) and transcendence. The Imam’s description of God as 'eternal, established, and existing' without limit or peer underscores the Shia theological stance on divine simplicity, directly linking to the Quranic verse 'There is nothing like unto Him' (42:11). This minimal knowledge serves as the prerequisite for deeper spiritual insight and correct worship.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. Muhammad ibn `Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim said, on the authority of Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn Mukhtar al-Hamdani, on the authority of al-Fath ibn Yazid al-Jurjani

that I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Kadhim (AS) about the least that is required to recognize Divine Unity. Thus, he (AS) replied, “the confirmation that there is no god other than Him. He has no peer or rival. He is Eternal without beginning. He is the Firm, the Existent, and is never Absent. There is nothing whatsoever like unto Him.”
